Not a bug, but potentially confusing for the owner — recommend defaulting crypto.enabled=true on fresh install since Phase 1 is now live-ready.

issues: React console warning: 'A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled' on the fee-percent inputs — happens when crypto.fees is initially undefined for a coin then filled. Cosmetic (default value fallback would fix it: value={crypto.fees?.[coin] ?? 4}).

React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — caused by Emergent's x-excluded instrumentation span being injected into <option> elements. This is instrumentation-only, not a product bug.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2276 lines (up from 2155). The fee arithmetic (_apply_fee/_crypto_fee_pct) and the reconcile/webhook branches for deposit+link_payment duplicate the same 20-line block twice. Extract into a single helper `finalize_crypto_credit(kind, doc, intent_id, tx_hash)` returning gross/fee/net and updating balance+txn+link_counters — will cut ~80 lines and remove drift risk.

The balance check at line 390 runs BEFORE the crypto asset/regex validation (line 522+). This means a user with insufficient balance sees 'Solde insuffisant' even for a syntactically invalid coin/address, obscuring the real error. Move asset+address validation ahead of the balance check for better UX.

biz_to_crypto uses `fee_pct = float(fees_map.get(coin_upper, 4.0)) / 100.0` (division by 100 to make it a ratio), then stores `fee_pct * 100` in metadata. Elsewhere (_apply_fee) `fee_pct` is stored as-is (4.0 not 0.04). This inconsistency (ratio vs percent) is a foot-gun for downstream reporting — pick one convention and document.

/api/crypto/coins returns `min`/`max` per network but the frontend BizToCryptoForm doesn't use them — user can submit an amount above IziPay's asset limit and only get the vendor rejection later. Consider client-side min/max validation.

_NETWORK_REGEX is defined AFTER the /crypto/coins endpoint uses it (line 1687 vs 1670). Python hoists top-level names via module scope so this works at runtime, but it's confusing — move regex map above endpoint.

No cleanup for the fresh test merchants created by /api/auth/register in test runs (iter11 leaves iter11_XXXX@test.com users behind). Consider adding a teardown or scoping via admin/users/cleanup-test-users.
Persistent from iter10: server.py should be split into routers (auth, transfers, admin, crypto, webhooks, notifications).
